label: bounded evidence, not proof
note: Open / conjectural statements checked on bounded ranges. 'verified' is the colony's OWN machine-checked range (starts empty). 'literature' is an informational pointer, not verified by the colony. Passing a range is bounded evidence, never proof; a counterexample candidate is independently re-checked, flagged loudly and frozen for human review — never claimed.

targets.statement: Every even n >= 4 is a sum of two primes (Goldbach).
targets.literature: Published computations report verification far beyond this range (e.g. Oliveira e Silva, Herzog & Pardi, to 4·10^18).
targets.label: bounded evidence, not proof

targets.statement: Every n >= 1 reaches 1 under n→n/2, 3n+1 (checked as: each n drops below itself; stopping-time record kept).
targets.literature: Published computations report verification far beyond this range (e.g. Barina, to 2^68).
targets.label: bounded evidence, not proof

targets.statement: For every n >= 1 there is a prime strictly between n^2 and (n+1)^2 (Legendre).
targets.literature: Implied far beyond this range by published prime-gap computations; open in general.
targets.label: bounded evidence, not proof

targets.statement: No composite n has phi(n) dividing n - 1 (Lehmer's totient problem).
targets.literature: Published work rules out small counterexamples (e.g. Cohen & Hagis: any counterexample has many prime factors); open in general.
targets.label: bounded evidence, not proof

targets.statement: For every n >= 2, 4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z has a solution in positive integers (Erdős–Straus).
targets.literature: Published computer searches reach far beyond this range; open in general.
targets.label: bounded evidence, not proof

targets.statement: pi_2(x) ~ 2·C_2·Li_2(x) (Hardy–Littlewood twin-prime estimate); checked as a consistency ratio at growing x — deviations are flags, never counterexamples.
targets.literature: Asymptotic conjecture; finite counts can only be consistent or inconsistent with it, never decide it.
targets.label: bounded evidence, not proof
